transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… occupational health at work asked me to come in. They’re saying my weight is dangerously low, especially with me running presses and doing fabrication all day. I guess I thought I was just getting leaner, more disciplined, you know? But they seemed pretty concerned, so… I’m here.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m trying to be difficult or anything. But yes, I do get scared. If the scale goes up even a little, I sort of panic, like I’m going to lose all the control I’ve worked so hard for and end up heavy again. I know that probably sounds extreme… but that’s what happens in my head.
Do you think your weight is currently low, or do you see yourself as overweight even though others are telling you that you are underweight?

I… I know other people are saying I’m underweight, and I guess I can hear that. But when I actually look at myself, like in the bathroom mirror or even a shop window at work, I don’t see it that way. I just get stuck on my stomach and my thighs, like they look too big, and then I feel awful about myself for the rest of the day. I know that probably isn’t the answer I’m supposed to give, but… that’s honestly what happens.
Do you often limit the amount or type of food you eat to avoid gaining weight?

I mean… I try to keep it sensible, or at least that’s how I tell myself it is. Most days before the early shift I’ll just have coffee, then maybe half a protein bar at lunch, and after yoga I’ll do a small bowl of vegetables. Eating more than that just makes the whole day feel… out of control. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?

I don’t think so… not in the way people usually mean, like a lot of food all at once. Sometimes I feel like I’ve eaten too much even if it’s not actually much, if that makes sense. But I wouldn’t say I have episodes where I’m eating a huge amount quickly. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve felt really uncomfortable after eating, but I don’t make myself throw up. I know that’s probably something you need to ask, but… no, not really.
Do you exercise to burn off calories or prevent weight gain?

I wouldn’t say it’s just to “burn off” calories exactly… I mean, exercise helps me feel like I’ve kept things in check. If the scale goes up even a little, I get really panicky, like I’m going to lose all the control I’ve worked so hard for and end up heavy again. So… yes, I guess I do use it to stop that from happening. Is that… does that make sense?
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating?

I’m not sure I’d call it “lost control.” I mean… I don’t really have those moments where I’m just eating and can’t stop, at least not that I can think of. Sometimes I feel upset after, like I shouldn’t have eaten something, but it’s not like I’m out of control exactly. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?

I don’t think so… not what I’d consider a large amount. I mean, sometimes I worry I’ve eaten too much, but if you mean a lot of food all at once, like quickly, I don’t really have episodes like that. I hope that answers it the right way.
Do you ever feel like you're eating much more quickly than usual during these times when you're worried about eating too much?

I don’t think so… I mean, I haven’t really noticed eating faster than usual. If anything, I’m usually pretty aware of what I’m doing when I eat. But maybe I’m not thinking about the speed exactly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you think your body shape or weight is the main thing that determines your self-worth?

I guess… I don’t want to say it’s the main thing, because that sounds really shallow or bad. But it does affect me a lot. Like if I catch myself in a shop window or in the bathroom mirror, I just zero in on my stomach or my thighs and think they look too big, and then it can kind of ruin how I feel about myself for the rest of the day. Is that what you mean?
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you didn't think your stomach and thighs looked too big?

I think… yes, probably. I mean, I wish I could say it’s only because of how those parts look, but if the scale goes up even a little, I get really panicky. Like I’m going to lose all the control I’ve worked so hard for and end up heavy again. I know that maybe sounds dramatic… but that’s honestly what it feels like.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered excessive in a short period of time, even if it was just once?

I… I don’t think so. Not in the way that sounds, anyway. I mean, sometimes I might feel like I ate “too much,” but that could be something other people would probably think is normal, so I’m not sure it counts. I wouldn’t want to exaggerate it.
Have you ever felt like you ate a normal or small amount of food, but still felt uncomfortably full afterwards?

I’m not really sure. I mean… I can feel full sometimes after eating, but I don’t know if it’s “uncomfortably” full, or if I’m just paying too much attention to it. I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. What would count as that?
Have you ever felt like you couldn't stop eating once you started?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, once I decide I’m done, I can usually stop. Sometimes I worry that I might not, if that makes sense, but I can’t think of a time where I truly couldn’t stop eating once I started. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever feel like you're eating without being able to stop once you've started, even if it's not a lot of food?

I don’t think so… I mean, not in a “I can’t stop” way. Sometimes I might feel a little nervous once I’ve started eating, like I’m watching myself too closely, but I can still stop. I’m sorry if that’s not a very clear answer.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered excessive, even if it was just one time?

I don’t think so… not what I would call excessive. I mean, I might feel like I ate too much sometimes, but when I think about the actual amount, it probably wasn’t a lot. I’m sorry, I don’t know if that answers it the way you need.
Do you ever feel like you are eating an amount of food that is much larger than what most people would eat in a similar time period?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes it feels like a lot to me, but if I picture what other people would eat in the same amount of time, I don’t think it would be more than that. Maybe less, honestly. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you ever had an episode where you felt like you were eating an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

I don’t think I’ve had an episode like that, no. I mean… I can feel like it was too much because I get anxious about it, but I don’t think it was an unusually large amount in a short time. At least not compared to what most people would mean by that.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt like you lost control while eating?

I’m not sure I’d call it losing control… I mean, I get upset with myself sometimes, or anxious while I’m eating, but I don’t think it’s like I can’t stop or I’m out of control. At least, not in the way I think you mean. Is that okay to say?
